question: For which architectural element is the Sidi Saiyyed Mosque in Gujarat famous for?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lattice windows (jalis)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sidi Saiyyed Mosque**, popularly known as **Sidi Saiyyed ni Jali**, was built in **1572-73 AD** in **Ahmedabad**, **Gujarat**.
 
• It was constructed by **Sidi Saiyyed**, an Abyssinian nobleman in the service of **Bilal Jhajhar Khan**, during the reign of the last Sultan of the **Gujarat Sultanate**, **Muzaffar Shah III**.
 
• The structure is world-famous for its ten beautifully carved semi-circular **lattice windows** (**jalis**) that adorn the side and rear arches of the mosque.
 
• The most iconic of these is the **Tree of Life** jali, which features a central tree with intertwining branches and foliage, showcasing unparalleled **Indo-Saracenic** craftsmanship.
 
• The delicate stone carving is so fine that it resembles **filigree** work, representing the height of the **Gujarat School of Architecture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Architectural Significance**:

 
 
• The **Tree of Life** design is the inspiration behind the logo of the **Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIMA)**.
 
• Unlike many other mosques of that era, the **Sidi Saiyyed Mosque** does not have a traditional courtyard, as it was built as part of the **citadel wall**.
 
• The central arch of the mosque is surprisingly devoid of a jali, likely due to the **Mughal invasion** of Gujarat in **1573** by **Emperor Akbar**, which halted the completion of the work.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Heritage**:
 
 
• The mosque is considered one of the finest examples of **Islamic art** in India, blending local **Hindu** and **Jain** motifs with Islamic architectural geometry.
 
• The city of **Ahmedabad**, where the mosque is located, was declared India's first **UNESCO World Heritage City** in **2017**.
